verdict.root_cause: The ad service is not running. Its own logs end with a clean JVM-initiated gRPC server shutdown at 10:47:51 followed by total silence and no startup banner [tr_049f5c41df79], and its span-metrics series returns no samples at all — neither error nor total spans — in the incident window [tr_cf83f6da7194]. The ad change log shows seven platform-automation image-reference changes in the ~1.2 hours before onset, alternating every 11-13 minutes between an unset reference and a single hotfix tag, the last an update to that hotfix tag ~5 minutes before onset [tr_e6ff75165b3e]: the deploy loop tore the running instance down and the hotfix artifact never came back up. Frontend is the reporter, not the culprit — all its errors are gRPC status 14 UNAVAILABLE with connect EHOSTUNREACH to a single peer 172.18.0.19:9555, no connection ever established [tr_9129eb349cc8], the traces show the frontend→AdService/GetAds client span as a childless leaf with no server-side ad span while cart, product-catalog and recommendation paths complete cleanly [tr_bead95082f1d], and frontend has no change records at all [tr_73b63a0cebf6].
verdict.reasoning: Ad's logs, metrics and traces all say the same thing: the process is absent, not erroring — orderly shutdown then silence [tr_049f5c41df79], an undefined error ratio with no denominator rather than a computed zero [tr_cf83f6da7194], and no server-side span for the frontend's ad call [tr_bead95082f1d]. Callers see a vanished endpoint: host-unreachable at connect time against one address, not a deadline, which excludes dependency_latency and overload [tr_9129eb349cc8]. It also excludes process_freeze, where the socket would still accept and callers would hang. Frontend is cleared by its empty change log [tr_73b63a0cebf6] and by its other dependencies being healthy in the same traces [tr_bead95082f1d]. The act upstream is the automation loop flapping ad's image reference, with the last update landing ~5 minutes before onset [tr_e6ff75165b3e]; only one tag is ever involved, so this is deployed-versus-not-deployed. The running artifact is not the one that should be running — bad_deploy — and the fix is to halt the flapping loop and restore ad to a known-good image that actually starts.
open_questions: Why the hotfix image never started after 10:47:53 — no orchestrator or pod-event evidence was gathered, so pull failure, crash before first log line, or the deploy never being applied are all still open.
Whether 172.18.0.19:9555 is ad's current endpoint or a stale address from the prior instance; the peer was identified only by IP, never resolved to a service name.
Why identical ad-path failures already appear at ~10:02 and ~10:29, well before the 10:53:31 alert — the flapping loop plausibly explains it but was not directly correlated against those timestamps.

alternatives.root_cause: The ad deployment's image reference was left pointing at an unset/invalid value by the automation loop, so no workload could be scheduled.
alternatives.why_not: The last recorded change set the reference to a concrete hotfix tag rather than unsetting it [tr_e6ff75165b3e], so at onset the configured artifact existed and simply failed to run — an artifact problem, not a wrong value.

alternatives.root_cause: The ad instance is alive but cut off at the network layer, so callers cannot reach it.
alternatives.why_not: A partitioned-but-running ad would keep logging and keep emitting spans; instead it logged a graceful shutdown and then emitted nothing at all [tr_049f5c41df79][tr_cf83f6da7194].

proposal.expected_effect: Nothing changes: ad keeps emitting no span-metrics samples and no log lines, and frontend keeps logging gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE / EHOSTUNREACH to 172.18.0.19:9555 at several lines per second. Any change in those signals without an operator acting means this brief is incomplete.
proposal.if_wrong: Overturn this if: (1) change history names a real prior image tag for ad other than the single hotfix tag - [tr_e6ff75165b3e] records the prior value as unset/None and only one tag ever appears, so rollback_image's precondition is met only by an absence, not a version; (2) orchestrator or container-event evidence shows the hotfix image pulls fine and the container was simply never recreated, which would make restart_service the right proposal; (3) evidence shows the platform-automation loop has stopped - as recorded it rewrote ad's image reference seven times at 11-13 minute intervals, so anything recreated now is likely torn down within a cycle.
proposal.risk: Abstaining leaves ad down and the ad path failing. But rollback_image would most likely set ad's image reference back to unset, turning a stopped container into one with no image and losing the only pointer to the hotfix artifact. restart_service would recreate ad at a tag whose startup has never been observed in logs [tr_049f5c41df79]; if it cannot pull or dies pre-logging, the attempt is wasted and the timeline is muddied. Neither touches the automation loop, which is the actual mechanism and is outside this executor.
proposal.blast_radius: Unchanged. Frontend remains the only observed caller of ad and continues to serve ~91-96% of calls successfully; cart, product-catalog and recommendation paths are unaffected either way.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerts on frontend and its proxy simultaneously affect the user-facing entry path, and no open incident covers them. Cause could be in the frontend itself or any of six downstream dependencies, so evidence is needed.
